news.title: World Cup stars drive record Sh1.3 trillion mid-year transfer window
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup has had a major impact on the global football transfer market, with 267 players who featured at this year’s tournament moving to new clubs during the mid-year transfer window. The players, drawn from 47 nationalities, were involved in transfers worth more than $3.3 billion (Sh427.2 billion) in combined fees between June 1 and September 2, according to FIFA’s International Transfer Snapshot released on Thursday. The figure came during a record-breaking window for men’s football, with clubs spending more than $9.89 billion (Sh1.3 trillion) on international transfer fees, the highest amount ever recorded for a mid-year window. More than 12,500 international transfers were also registered worldwide, setting another record.

news.title: After Winning FIFA World Cup, 31-Year-Old Spainard Announces Retirement
news.lede: Marcos Llorente has announced his retirement from international football at the age of 31, bringing his six-year Spain career to an unexpected end just weeks after helping the country win the World Cup. The Atletico Madrid midfielder revealed his decision in a surprise social media post on Thursday. “After turning the decision over in my mind for a long time, I have decided to bring my time with the national team to a close,” posted Llorente. Llorente was part of Spain’s World Cup-winning squad in July, serving as back-up to Tottenham’s Pedro Porro at right back.

news.title: How Will Argentina Honor Messi After Retirement? AFA Reveals
news.lede: TEMPO.CO, Jakarta - The Argentine Football Association (AFA) will pay tribute to Lionel Messi during all Argentine league matches this weekend following the football superstar's retirement from international duty.As a tribute to Messi's career with the Argentina national team, referees will stop play in the 10th minute of every match, the AFA said in a statement quoted by The Athletic on Thursday, September 3." We look forward to seeing you on the fields – join us in this recognition!" the association saidm as quoted by beIN Sports.Messi, who famously wore the No. 10 shirt for Argentina, announced his retirement from international football on Monday, August 31. His final appearance for La Albiceleste came in the 2026 World Cup final against Spain in July.The 39-year-old ended his international career as Argentina's most-capped player, making 207 appearances.

news.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of 'smear campaign' against Infantino
news.lede: The dispute between the two football associations reached a US court, in which UEFA is looking for permission to collect evidence for criminal proceedings in Switzerland. World football governing body FIFA took a lash at Europe's UEFA for starting a "smear campaign" and "fishing expedition" against FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino. This comes after a dispute between the two organizations due to FIFA's plan to sell a stake in its commercial rights, with UEFA submitting an ex parte application to the US District Court in New York to obtain testimony and documents from US-based entities. These documents will be used in potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, where both FIFA and UEFA are based.

news.title: A house divided: HKFA staying silent with Asia still split on Infantino’s future
news.lede: While the famously taciturn Football Association of Hong Kong, China is refusing to pick a side, elsewhere in Asia battle lines are being drawn between those that support Fifa president Gianni Infantino and those who want him kicked out of the game. With little more than two months to go before the deadline to nominate a challenger in next year’s election, a look at who stands where shows a region deeply divided, with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) aligning with its counterparts in Europe and North America, but in direct opposition to some of its member nations. Having stayed tight-lipped since Infantino’s plan to sell off the World Cup to private investors was exposed, the HKFA this week told the South China Morning Post that they had “noted the recent discussions regarding Fifa Forward Enterprise [FFE]” and had “no available information to be released at this stage”.

news.title: ‘Smear campaign’: Football civil war reignites as FIFA hits back at UEFA’s Infantino threat
news.lede: FIFA has accused UEFA of a “smear campaign” and a “fishing expedition” after European football’s governing body asked US judges to force it to hand over documents related to its failed World Cup investor plan. The global football body’s divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to investors, unveiled in July, triggered a huge backlash across the sport, with UEFA threatening to boycott the World Cup unless the plan was scrapped.
